title: Singapore property value: today's prices and future values by town and type
scope: Today's typical price of a home in 26 Singapore towns, for HDB 2-room, 3-room, 4-room, 5-room and executive flats, executive condominiums, condominiums or apartments and landed houses, with what it could be worth in 1 to 20 years at a low, base or high yearly rate. HDB prices are official transaction data: the median of all resales registered with HDB on data.gov.sg over Nov 2025 to Oct 2026, with the three 12-month windows before it. Private-property price trends are official: URA's private residential price indices (landed; non-landed in the CCR, RCR and OCR) to Q3 2026. Private prices today are researched estimates: mostly URA-caveat median prices per sq ft by postal district or project, as reported by PropertyNet, EdgeProp, PropKaki, SRX and similar sites in 2026, multiplied by an assumed size (condo 1,000 sq ft, EC 1,100 sq ft, terrace about 1,800 sq ft of land). The base rate is each item's compound yearly change over the last 3 years; low and high are the weakest and strongest of those years. Prices are in Singapore dollars, before stamp duties, legal fees, agent fees and renovation.
limits: Projections are scenarios, not forecasts: they assume a past 3-year rate carries on, and prices can rise more slowly or fall (cooling measures, interest rates and supply all move them). HDB figures are town medians, so the mix of blocks, floors and remaining lease sold each year moves them; your flat's price will differ, and older leases tend to rise more slowly or fall. Private prices today are estimates, not official statistics: most are district medians that cover more than one town, and a few (marked 'estimate') rest on listings or a handful of sales. Private items share URA's regional or landed index for their past values and rates, so two towns in the same region project at the same rate. EC figures mix older privatised ECs and newer ones still under resale limits. Landed figures are typical terraces, except Sembawang (semi-D); there is no figure where a town has no landed estate or too few sales. Not included: taxes, fees, rental income, financing costs and Cash-Over-Valuation.

options.rationale: About 60 to 70 sqm. Official data: median of all 3-room resales in the town registered with HDB (data.gov.sg).

options.label: HDB 4-room
options.rationale: About 90 sqm, the most traded flat type and the default. Official data: median of all 4-room resales in the town registered with HDB (data.gov.sg).

options.label: HDB 5-room
options.rationale: About 110 to 120 sqm. Official data: median of all 5-room resales in the town registered with HDB (data.gov.sg).

options.label: HDB executive flat
options.rationale: About 130 to 150 sqm, no longer built, so supply is fixed. Official data: median of all executive-flat resales in the town registered with HDB (data.gov.sg).

options.label: Executive condominium (EC)
options.rationale: Researched estimate for a 1,100 sq ft EC unit, from URA-caveat-based psf figures reported by property portals (2026). Past prices and rates follow URA's OCR non-landed index, since ECs are all outside the central region.

options.label: Condominium or apartment
options.rationale: Researched estimate for a 1,000 sq ft resale condo, mostly the postal-district median psf from URA caveats as reported by property portals (Oct 2025 to Sep 2026). Past prices and rates follow URA's index for the item's region (CCR, RCR or OCR).

options.label: Landed house
options.rationale: Researched estimate for a typical terrace (usually 1,800 sq ft of land; the item notes say when it is a semi-D or a listing-based estimate). Past prices and rates follow URA's island-wide landed index.
